title: Documentation Standards for Blood Glucose Testing Supplies: Written Orders and Prior Authorization
content:
These standards govern the paperwork every Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program shipment rests on.

**1. The written order.** Every shipment rests on a written order from the treating prescriber that names the item, the billing units per 30 days, the order date and the prescriber's NPI. The order is valid for the tier's order validity, in calendar months counted from its order date, the valid-through date being the day before the same calendar day that many months later (falling back to the last day of the month when that day does not exist), and Larkfield records that valid-through date when the order is received.

**2. Tiers with prior authorization.** On tiers where prior authorization is required, Larkfield submits a prior authorization request to the payer once the written order is on file and moves the program from referral received to pending authorization. The payer's approval is recorded as an authorization grant with the basis payer prior authorization, carrying the payer's PA reference, the approved units and the approved span. The span runs the tier's prior authorization validity, in calendar months from the decision date, unless the payer's approval states an earlier valid-through date, in which case the payer's date governs.

**3. Tiers without prior authorization.** On tiers where prior authorization is not required, Larkfield records the authorization grant itself on the basis of the written order (basis written order, or self-pay order on the self-pay tier), valid from the order date through the order's valid-through date, for the billing units the order covers within that span.

**4. Standard and expedited requests.** A prior authorization request is submitted as expedited only when the prescriber states on the order that waiting the standard decision time could seriously jeopardize the patient's life or health; otherwise it is standard. The payer is expected to decide within the tier's standard decision time, in calendar days of a standard request, or its expedited decision time, in hours of an expedited one.

**5. Renewal.** A renewal request for a prior authorization may be submitted no earlier than the tier's renewal lead, in calendar days before the valid-through date of the authorization it renews, counted backward in calendar days from that valid-through date with the earliest submission day itself allowed, and it requires a written order that is valid beyond that valid-through date. Both facts are read from the authorization and order records.

**6. Activation.** A program is activated only when an authorization grant on file for the program is valid on the activation date.

**7. Denial of a prior authorization.** A payer denial of a prior authorization is recorded with the payer's denial reason; the program stays in pending authorization while the prescriber supplies further documentation or a new request is made, and it closes only under the program hold and closure rules.

**8. Clinical documents.** Clinical documents are recorded with the purpose they serve and the visit date they document, and a document serves only the purpose recorded on it.

**Worked dates (hypothetical)**

- An order dated 15 March on a tier with a 12-month order validity is valid through 14 March of the following year.
- An authorization valid through 30 June on a tier with a 21-day renewal lead may be renewed from 9 June: a request on 9 June is allowed, a request on 8 June is too early. The renewal also needs a written order valid after 30 June.
- An authorization grant valid from 1 April through 30 September supports activation on any day from 1 April to 30 September inclusive, and on no other day.
